lines.text: The human skeleton is the framework that supports and protects the body. An adult skeleton contains 206 bones, divided into the axial skeleton (skull, spine, and ribcage) and the appendicular skeleton (arms, legs, shoulders, and hips). The skull protects the brain and gives shape to the face. Below it, the spine — a column of 33 vertebrae — runs from the neck to the tailbone, protecting the spinal cord. The ribcage shields the heart and lungs, anchored to the sternum at the front. The collarbone and shoulder blade form the shoulder girdle, while the pelvis supports the lower body. Bones connect at joints, held together by ligaments. Cartilage cushions the joints and prevents bones from grinding together. Inside the bone, marrow produces blood cells. The skeleton also stores minerals like calcium, which keeps bones strong. The periosteum is a thin membrane covering each bone's surface. A fracture occurs when a bone breaks, and a dislocation happens when a bone slips out of its joint. Understanding the skeleton helps us appreciate how the body moves — every step, turn, and stretch depends on bones, joints, and the connective tissue that links them.
